architecture.mechanism: Lightweight metallic materials (steel, aluminum, titanium, magnesium alloys) for automotive body panels enable mass-production vehicles with reduced mass, which lowers electrical load demand on the battery and alternator during cranking and standby operation, thereby reducing susceptibility to parasitic-drain-induced depletion.
architecture.intervention: Inspect the 2021 Mazda CX-5 for any non-OEM lightweight alloy body panels, aluminum hood, or magnesium seat frames introduced via service-replacement that may house or contact wiring harnesses, ground points, or the battery negative cable, and verify that all chassis-to-body ground straps at these alloy interfaces are intact, correctly torqued, and free of galvanic-corrosion-induced high resistance; then perform a standardized parasitic-draw clamp-on measurement and voltage-drop test across each ground strap and the battery negative cable with the vehicle undisturbed for the documented 1-day soak period.
architecture.expected_effect: A localized abnormal parasitic draw (≥50 mA) or excessive ground-circuit resistance (>0.1 V drop) is identified without needing to reproduce the no-start event, confirming whether metallic-panel/ground-strap degradation is the root cause of the sudden depletion.
architecture.falsification_test: If every aluminum/magnesium/steel panel-to-chassis ground point measures <0.1 V drop at the key-off state, total quiescent current remains within Mazda's published ≤30 mA specification, and the battery holds ≥12.4 V after the 1-day soak, then lightweight-material-induced parasitic draw is excluded as the mechanism.
